text: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: he was forming a swarm of locusts just as the late crop was beginning to come up—the late crop that follows the king's mowings.

versions.text: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: he was forming locusts just as the late crop was beginning to come up—the late crop that follows the king's mowings.
versions.explanation: גֹּבַי is a collective noun for a locust swarm; "a swarm of locusts" makes the image vivid and clarifies the collective sense that "they" in verse 2 refers back to.

text: And when they had finished devouring the vegetation of the land, I said, "Lord GOD, forgive, I pray! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "It shall not be," said the LORD.
This is what the Lord GOD showed me: behold, the Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep and began to devour the farmland.

versions.text: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: the Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was consuming the land.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew הַחֵלֶק means "the portion/allotted farmland," not simply "the land" (הָאָרֶץ, used elsewhere in the chapter). Rendering it "the farmland" preserves the distinction and avoids repeating the same English word for two different Hebrew terms. "Began to devour" also reads more smoothly than the mixed tenses of "was consuming."

versions.text: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: the Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep and began to devour the farmland.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew וְהִנֵּה ("and behold") marks the vision's sudden appearance and is a recurring feature of the vision reports in this chapter. Rendering it keeps the dramatic force for oral reading; the present text silently omits it.

text: Then I said, "Lord GOD, stop, I pray! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "This also shall not be," said the Lord GOD.
This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing by a wall built with a plumb line, and in his hand was a plumb line.
And the LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "See, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel; I will spare them no longer.

versions.text: And the LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "See, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel; I will never again pass them by.
versions.explanation: "Pass them by" is ambiguous in modern English—a hearer may take it to mean the opposite (that God will always come to them). The idiom here means to overlook or forgive, so "I will spare them no longer" conveys the sense clearly for oral reading.

text: The high places of Isaac shall be laid waste and the sanctuaries of Israel shall lie in ruins, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos is plotting against you in the very midst of the house of Israel. The land cannot endure all his words.
For this is what Amos has said: 'Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away into exile from its own land.'"
And Amaziah said to Amos, "Go away, seer! Flee to the land of Judah. Eat your bread there, and prophesy there.
But never prophesy again at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary and a royal temple."
Then Amos answered Amaziah, "I am no prophet, nor the son of a prophet. I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'
Now then, hear the word of the LORD. You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel; do not preach against the house of Isaac.'

Therefore this is what the LORD says: 'Your wife shall become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and daughters shall fall by the sword. Your land shall be divided up with a measuring line, and you yourself shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall surely be led away into exile from its own land.'"
